title: 一度に — all at once
summary: An adverbial phrase meaning to do or have many things at the same moment or in a single go. It suits large amounts or simultaneous events.

body.p: 一度 means one time and に marks the manner. 一度に～する means doing something in a single go or at the same time. It fits actions with large amounts or many people: eating a lot, coming in, clearing tasks.
同時に stresses that two or more things happen at once; 一度に stresses doing it all in one go. In negatives (一度にはできない) it means 'it can't be done in one go.'

examples.ja: そんなに一度（いちど）にたくさん食（た）べられません。
examples.romaji: Sonna ni ichido ni takusan taberaremasen.
examples.tr: I can't eat so much all at once.

examples.ja: 大勢（おおぜい）のお客（きゃく）が一度（いちど）に店（みせ）に入（はい）ってきた。
examples.romaji: Ōzei no okyaku ga ichido ni mise ni haitte kita.
examples.tr: A crowd of customers came into the shop all at once.

examples.ja: たまった用事（ようじ）を一度（いちど）に片付（かたづ）けてしまおう。
examples.romaji: Tamatta yōji o ichido ni katazukete shimaō.
examples.tr: Let's take care of all the piled-up errands all at once.

pitfalls: 一度に is different from plain 一度 (once, as in 日本に一度行った).
It does not mean 'only one time' but 'together, in one go.'
